source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus holds 36 MW of IT capacity, the fourth-largest published data center in Texas, translating to roughly 900 racks at typical AI training density.

This facility was designed for enterprise and cloud workloads before the recent acceleration in AI demand. Its 296,000 square feet of technical space and compliance certifications for healthcare, government, and payment systems suggest a mature multi-building campus optimized for regulated tenants rather than accelerator-dense training clusters. The operator publishes no tenant mix or utilization data, so whether these 36 MW currently serve AI workloads or run at what density remains undisclosed.

The campus qualifies to host regulated workloads, which constrains deployment flexibility but does not prevent AI use. FISMA, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and other certifications indicate customers whose workloads demand compliance controls, not performance optimization. No power infrastructure details are published, leaving critical unknowns: whether 36 MW reflects the total campus power delivery capacity, backup generation capability, or only IT equipment limits. Grid connection capacity and whether the facility can sustain the sustained high-power draw of accelerator clusters are invisible.

Texas data centers represent 7.6 percent of the state's published 475 MW across 19 disclosed facilities, yet 133 mapped locations exist statewide. Most Texas data centers do not publish capacity specifications, meaning scaling constraints in the state are largely invisible to outsiders. This campus matters to AI deployment only if its power infrastructure and density match emerging workload requirements, which the available data does not establish.
